description: Verify the rules a repo states in its context files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules, ...) against its code. Read those files, then map each rule-like sentence to one template, quoting it exactly. archprint checks the quote is in the file and the mapping matches real files, measures how many files follow or break it, and returns a gap report: enforce now, enforce with a baseline (broken today, with the files), already an archprint rule, check the mapping, or guidance only. Show the report to the user: adopting a rule is their decision. Templates, with globs relative to `path` in ESLint syntax: "forbid-import" (files must not import `targets`, path globs matched on the file an import resolves to, or `packages`, specifier globs, each optionally limited to named `imports` such as {"name": "next/cache", "imports": ["unstable_cache"]}); "forbid-usage" (files must not use a global named in `usage`, such as "fetch", "window" or "process.env"); "forbid-file" (no new file may match `files`); "inferred" (the sentence is a rule archprint_scan lists; `rule` is its id); "none" (no template fits; give the `reason`, e.g. a style rule a standard linter covers). Read-only.

name.description: for forbid-*: lowercase words joined by "-", e.g. no-fetch-in-components

reason.description: for none: why no template fits

rule.description: for inferred: the archprint rule id

path.description: repository root on this machine, where the context files are (default "."), not a URL

name: archprint_gap_report
title: Verify the rules in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
